# Projected products in the prompt's unshifted normalization

Ziegler's projected deformed products give a substantially larger benchmark than the elementary product barrier in the previous attempt. The imported realization theorem applies to even$n\ge4$ and$r\ge2$: certain deformed products of$r$ $n$-gons project to convex4-polytopes preserving their graph. Proposition5.1 supplies cubical and prismatic facet counts. No new coordinate realization is claimed here.

Write$N=n^r$. The checked source data are
\[
f_0=N,\quad f_1=rN,\quad
C=(r-2)N/4,\quad P=rN/n,
\]
where$C$ counts cube facets and$P$ counts$n$-gonal prisms. Counting each ridge twice gives the remaining entries independently:
\[
f_3=C+P,\qquad
f_2=3C+(n+2)P/2
=\left((5r-6)/4+r/n\right)N.
\]
Indeed a cube has six ridges and an$n$-prism has$n+2$. These equations also satisfy$f_0-f_1+f_2-f_3=0$ exactly, checking the normalization without depending on damaged extracted subscripts.

For the literal unshifted ratio, direct substitution yields
\[
\phi=\frac{9rn-6n+4r}{rn+2n+4r}.
\]
Choose$n=2r$, always an admissible even integer. Then
\[
\phi=\frac{9r-4}{r+4}=9-\frac{40}{r+4}.
\]
For every$\varepsilon>0$, any integer$r\ge2$ with$r+4>40/\varepsilon$ supplies a credited convex example of ratio greater than$9-\varepsilon$. This is not unbounded fatness, and it does not require equal vertex and facet counts.
